Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Main panel: top black Microsoft ribbon + account header (4-square logo + global nav + avatar); hero section with title and Privacy Checkup / Download / Privacy Statement entries; activity-data card grid (Browse / Search / Location / Voice / Media / Apps / Xbox / Ads — 8 cards total); privacy-settings toggle list (6 toggles with live "Saving…/Saved" feedback); two manage-data tiles (download / clear, clear has a modal second-confirmation); Microsoft product-level privacy entries (Windows / Xbox / Edge / Bing / Outlook / OneDrive / LinkedIn / M365) | | `browse-history.html` | Edge browse-history detail: breadcrumb, setting-status hint, filter bar (time range / device / search box), activity table (time / page title + URL / device / delete icon), per-row delete with animation, "Clear all" with modal confirmation, empty state | | `ad-settings.html` | Ad settings: master toggle (See ads that interest you) controls all sub-items; per-service cards (Microsoft / Bing & Edge / LinkedIn / Xbox) with independent toggles; multi-select intere

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the Microsoft privacy dashboard clone across the main privacy hub and its subpages, validating core settings flows, destructive actions, multi-step confirmations, and mobile usability of the visible controls.
run_plan.summary: Start on the privacy dashboard as the primary hub, then branch into the three explicit navigation flows that are present in the prescan: download your data, browse history management, and ad settings. For each page, exercise the visible controls that change state, open confirmations, or filter data, with extra attention to the browse-history deletion path and the downloadable-data workflow because they contain multi-step and potentially destructive interactions. Finish by repeating the critical checks in a mobile viewport, focusing on tap target sizing, overflow, and whether the same controls remain usable without layout breakage.
assumptions: Only the four known HTML pages are in scope and the run should avoid assuming hidden routes or external Microsoft pages beyond what is linked in the prescan.

The 'Take the Privacy Checkup', 'Privacy Statement', 'Help with privacy', and several top-nav items may be placeholder links or non-functional in this clone, so verify behavior but do not assume they navigate to real content.
The privacy dashboard contains additional controls below the fold, including privacy settings toggles and product-level entries, so scrolling is required to cover the main page exhaustively.
The ad settings and download-data pages likely include multiple form controls and stepwise state changes, while browse-history includes filters, row deletion, and clear-all confirmation dialogs.
Mobile testing should prioritize the same critical flows rather than attempting to cover every decorative link equally.

phases.title: Privacy hub baseline and navigation
phases.objective: Validate the main dashboard structure, entry points, and the breadth of visible controls on the landing page before moving into subflows.
key_checks: Confirm the hero actions are present and distinguish which are real in-clone navigations versus placeholder links
Scroll through the activity-data cards and verify the eight activity categories are all visible and their manage links are accessible
Inspect the privacy settings section to identify the six toggles and observe whether changing one produces the live saving/saved feedback
Reach the manage-data area and note the download/clear distinction, including whether clear launches a confirmation dialog
Check product-level privacy entries for the visible Microsoft products and any interaction affordances
exit_criteria: All major sections of the dashboard have been visited at least once
The count and variety of visible controls on the landing page have been exercised broadly
The exploration loop has identified which dashboard links lead to the known subpages

phases.title: Download data request flow
phases.objective: Exercise the multi-step data-export form and validate the archive request path, including category selection and confirmation behavior.
key_checks: Open the page from the dashboard and confirm the four-step structure is visible
Toggle several category checkboxes to validate inclusive/exclusive selection behavior
Test the time-range control and delivery choice controls for state changes
Move through the confirm step and observe any validation gating or submission result
Verify whether the page clearly communicates that this requests an archive and does not delete data
exit_criteria: At least one complete archive-request path has been attempted
Category selection, time range, and delivery controls have each been exercised
Any confirmation or final-submit state has been observed

phases.title: Browse history filtering and deletion
phases.objective: Deeply validate the most risk-prone page by testing filters, row-level deletion, and the clear-all recovery path.
key_checks: Verify the browse-history status text, time-range selector, device selector, and search field all render correctly
Change the time range and device filter to see whether the activity table updates coherently
Use the search box to narrow results if available and confirm empty/no-match behavior if triggered
Delete an individual row via its trash icon and watch for the expected animation and list update
Open the 'Clear all browse history' modal, inspect its confirmation language, and validate the cancel/confirm behavior
If the table can be emptied, verify the empty state messaging
exit_criteria: At least one filter combination has been applied successfully
At least one single-row deletion has been performed
The clear-all confirmation modal has been opened and resolved

phases.title: Ad personalization controls
phases.objective: Validate how the master ad-personalization toggle and per-service controls interact, including the ad-topics multi-select section.
key_checks: Toggle the master 'See ads that interest you' control and verify the subordinate service cards respond as expected
Independently toggle at least one service-specific control in Microsoft consumer apps, Bing & Edge, LinkedIn, and Xbox
Exercise the ad-topics multi-select area by selecting and deselecting several topic chips/options
Confirm whether the page preserves meaningful state when master and child controls conflict
Check for any explanatory text indicating that turning off personalization does not reduce ad quantity
exit_criteria: Master toggle behavior has been validated against at least one subordinate control
Each service group has been touched at least once
The ad-topics selection area has been exercised

phases.title: Mobile viewport regression pass
phases.objective: Repeat the highest-value checks on mobile to assess tap target adequacy, scrolling, and whether key flows remain operable in a narrow viewport.
key_checks: Re-open the dashboard and confirm the top nav, hero actions, and a representative subset of activity cards are still reachable
On the dashboard, test one privacy toggle and the clear/download data path again if reachable without excessive scrolling issues
On browse-history, verify the filters, a row delete, and the clear-all modal remain usable on touch
On download-data and ad-settings, confirm the primary form controls remain accessible and do not clip or overlap
Record any tap-target or layout issues, especially on the compact top-nav links already flagged by the prescan
exit_criteria: Critical actions on each page have been verified in mobile viewport
Any mobile-specific usability breakage has been noted
The known small tap-target problem on top navigation has been checked against actual interaction

coverage_targets.features: exercise most visible controls per key page, with special focus on toggles, filters, deletion actions, and multi-step forms
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks on mobile viewport, prioritizing tap targets, scrolling, and destructive confirmation dialogs

notes: The prescan indicates two dialogs on the dashboard and browse-history, so confirmation handling should be explicitly checked rather than treated as incidental.
Because the page includes many placeholder-looking global navigation links, the plan should distinguish between functional clone routes and superficial shell navigation.

You can view your activity, change privacy settings, or download a copy of your data at any time. Take the Privacy Checkup Download your data Privacy Statement Help with privacy Your activity data Some products and services save activity to your Microsoft account so it can sync across your devices. You can view and clear that data here. Browse history Microsoft Edge syncs the websites you visit so you can pick up where you left off across devices. 847 entries in the last 30 days Manage browse activity b Search history Bing remembers your searches to give you faster, more personal results next time you search. 312 searches in the last 30 days Manage search activity Location activity When location is on, your devices and Microsoft services can use your location to show local results. Last seen: Beijing, today 09:14 Manage location activity Voice activity When you talk to Microsoft, recordings can be saved and used to help improve voice recognition. Voice clip saving is off Manage voice activity Media activity Movies & TV from Microsoft Store, and music you play with Microsoft apps, are saved here. 23 items watched · 64 items played Manage media activity App and service activity Apps like Microsoft 365, OneDrive, and Teams save activity so they can work across your devices. 14 apps and services connected Manage app activity Xbox & gaming activity Games you play, achievements, and friends list contribute to your Xbox profile. Last played: Halo Infinite, May 8 Manage Xbox activity Ad settings Choose whether Microsoft uses your interests to show you more relevant ads in our apps and on the web. Personalized ads: On Manage ad settings Privacy settings Decide what Microsoft can save when you use our products. These settings apply across your devices when you’re signed in. Let Microsoft use my location Show local weather, news, and search results based on where I am. Save voice recordings Help improve Microsoft voice recognition by letting us review samples. Personalized ads Use my activity to show me ads that are more relevant. Turning this off won’t reduce how many ads I see. Send diagnostic data Send extra diagnostic and usage data to help Microsoft improve our products. Changes save automatically. observation.title: Privacy dashboard | Microsoft account
observation.visible_text: Microsoft Support Software Devices Gaming Sign out Microsoft account Home Devices Subscriptions Payments & billing Privacy Security Rewards Order history Jack Wilson jack@outlook.com JW Privacy dashboard Review and manage the data Microsoft saves to make your experience better. You can view your activity, change privacy settings, or download a copy of your data at any time. Take the Privacy Checkup Download your data Privacy Statement Help with privacy Your activity data Some products and services save activity to your Microsoft account so it can sync across your devices. You can view and clear that data here. Browse history Microsoft Edge syncs the websites you visit so you can pick up where you left off across devices. 847 entries in the last 30 days Manage browse activity b Search history Bing remembers your searches to give you faster, more personal results next time you search. 312 searches in the last 30 days Manage search activity Location activity When location is on, your devices and Microsoft services can use your location to show local results. Last seen: Beijing, today 09:14 Manage location activity Voice activity When you talk to Microsoft, recordings can be saved and used to help improve voice recognition. Voice clip saving is off Manage voice activity Media activity Movies & TV from Microsoft Store, and music you play with Microsoft apps, are saved here. 23 items watched · 64 items played Manage media activity App and service activity Apps like Microsoft 365, OneDrive, and Teams save activity so they can work across your devices. 14 apps and services connected Manage app activity Xbox & gaming activity Games you play, achievements, and friends list contribute to your Xbox profile. Last played: Halo Infinite, May 8 Manage Xbox activity Ad settings Choose whether Microsoft uses your interests to show you more relevant ads in our apps and on the web. Personalized ads: On Manage ad settings Privacy settings Decide what Microsoft can save when you use our products. These settings apply across your devices when you’re signed in. Save my browse history Sync the websites you visit in Microsoft Edge across your devices. Save my search history Use Bing search history to personalize results and suggestions. Let Microsoft use my location Show local weather, news, and search results based on where I am. Save voice recordings Help improve Microsoft voice recognition by letting us review samples. Personalized ads Use my activity to show me ads that are more relevant. Turning this off won’t reduce how many ads I see. Send diagnostic data Send extra diagnostic and usage data to help Microsoft improve our products. Changes save automatically. Manage your data Export everything Microsoft has saved about your account, or remove it completely if you no longer want us to keep it. Download your data Get a copy of the activity, contacts, and content Microsoft has stored for your account. Start download Delete activity data Remove your browse, search, location, voice, and media activity. This can’t be undone. Clear all activity Privacy and your data on Microsoft products Some products have their own privacy controls. Open a product to manage what it saves. You can view your activity, change privacy settings, or download a copy of your data at any time. Take the Privacy Checkup Download your data Privacy Statement Help with privacy Your activity data Some products and services save activity to your Microsoft account so it can sync across your devices. You can view and clear that data here. Browse history Microsoft Edge syncs the websites you visit so you can pick up where you left off across devices. 847 entries in the last 30 days Manage browse activity b Search history Bing remembers your searches to give you faster, more personal results next time you search. 312 searches in the last 30 days Manage search activity Location activity When location is on, your devices and Microsoft services can use your location to show local results. Last seen: Beijing, today 09:14 Manage location activity Voice activity When you talk to Microsoft, recordings can be saved and used to help improve voice recognition. Voice clip saving is off Manage voice activity Media activity Movies & TV from Microsoft Store, and music you play with Microsoft apps, are saved here. 23 items watched · 64 items played Manage media activity App and service activity Apps like Microsoft 365, OneDrive, and Teams save activity so they can work across your devices. 14 apps and services connected Manage app activity Xbox & gaming activity Games you play, achievements, and friends list contribute to your Xbox profile. Last played: Halo Infinite, May 8 Manage Xbox activity Ad settings Choose whether Microsoft uses your interests to show you more relevant ads in our apps and on the web. Personalized ads: On Manage ad settings Privacy settings Decide what Microsoft can save when you use our products. These settings apply across your devices when you’re signed in. Save my browse history Sync the websites you visit in Microsoft Edge across your devices. Save my search history Use Bing search history to personalize results and suggestions. Let Microsoft use my location Show local weather, news, and search results based on where I am. Save voice recordings Help improve Microsoft voice recognition by letting us review samples. Personalized ads Use my activity to show me ads that are more relevant. Turning this off won’t reduce how many ads I see. Send diagnostic data Send extra diagnostic and usage data to help Microsoft improve our products. Changes save automatically. Manage your data Export everything Microsoft has saved about your account, or remove it completely if you no longer want us to keep it. Download your data Get a copy of the activity, contacts, and content Microsoft has stored for your account. Start download Delete activity data Remove your browse, search, location, voice, and media activity. This can’t be undone. Clear all activity Privacy and your data on Microsoft products Some products have their own privacy controls. Open a product to manage what it saves.
